solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fit together with man in centre

indicators.note: in places the word for man inside the word for centre

parts.note: the core of something is its centre
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Advice on assembling something, with a man placed in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Parts that cohere stick together into a unified whole, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Number on tree to frighten source of lucre

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred
the ash is a common tree
to cow someone is to intimidate them

explanation.surface: A figure posted on a tree to scare people off a money source.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' simply places C above ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash cow is a business or product that reliably brings in money, an idiom.

clue.text: American novelist, string player, and general

parts.note: a harper plays the harp, a stringed instrument
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A list of an American writer, a musician and a military man.
explanation.definitionFit: Harper Lee was the Alabama author of a famous 1960 novel, so she is an example of an American novelist.

clue.text: Lawyers upset by a little furry animal

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: the bar is the collective name for barristers
a bit is a small amount

explanation.surface: Attorneys distressed by a small furry creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit is a familiar small furry mammal, an example of the category.

clue.text: Explorer with piece of paper mainly on people carrier

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a column is a regular article in a newspaper
a bus carries passengers

explanation.surface: An explorer riding a minibus with a sheet of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Columbus was the navigator who reached the Americas in 1492, an example of an explorer.

clue.text: The French bear is British

definitions.meaning: in French the word for a bear is the same four letters
to a Briton, things British are belonging to us

explanation.surface: A claim that the bear in France actually belongs to Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: French for bear gives one sense; the possessive pronoun meaning belonging to us gives the other.

clue.text: Turn shotgun loose that isn't wanted

parts.note: a U-turn, so U stands for turn

indicators.note: loose suggests the letters are set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: Releasing an unwelcome shotgun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsought is not looked for or desired, matching a thing nobody wants.

clue.text: Good guy dropped?

parts.note: a dependable person is called a ..., and to blunder is to drop one

explanation.surface: Has a decent fellow been let go?
explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang calls a reliable friend this, and making a gaffe is dropping one.

clue.text: New cakes and rounds from the man in the galley

indicators.note: new indicates the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: two round letters O

explanation.surface: Fresh cakes and rounds of drinks from the ship's kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Os sit among the shuffled letters of CAKES.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley is a ship's kitchen, and the person cooking in it is a sea cook.

clue.text: Writer of science has pruned currant

parts.note: sc. is an abbreviation for science

indicators.note: pruned means cut back, so the end is trimmed off

parts.note: Ribes is the botanical genus of currants

explanation.surface: A science writer has been cutting back a currant bush.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is a copyist or writer, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Balkan capital as good as new with new conclusion

indicators.note: a new conclusion means the final letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: pristine means in original, unspoiled condition

explanation.surface: A Balkan city restored like new, with a fresh ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Pristina is the capital of Kosovo, an example of a capital in the Balkans.

clue.text: See 21
One owed by councillor to journalist

parts.note: an editor is a senior journalist

explanation.surface: Someone owed money by a local councillor and a newspaper man.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditor is a person to whom money is owed, a dictionary sense.

clue.text: Bananas building no nest?

definitions.meaning: a certain bird lays eggs in other birds' nests rather than building its own

explanation.surface: Going mad because one has failed to make a nest.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird's name is also slang for mad, and it famously never builds a nest.

clue.text: Exclamation carrying some weight in backward county

indicators.note: carrying means the reversed county holds the weight inside it
backward means the county's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Herts is short for Hertfordshire, an English county north of London
wt is an abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: A cry from someone hauling a load around a backwater county.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewth is a dated British and Australian oath of surprise, derived from God's truth.

clue.text: Barrier with everybody

parts.note: all means every person

explanation.surface: A barrier that includes everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall is a structure that blocks passage, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Artist's vade mecum in second boat — reserve

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: An artist's handbook kept in the second boat, booked ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A vade mecum is a thing carried everywhere; an artist carries a pad for drawing.

clue.text: Servants ask to be served with romances

parts.note: in a restaurant you order food
to romance is to tell untrue stories, so romances are lies

explanation.surface: Domestic staff demanding service along with love stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderlies are attendants in hospitals or the army, a kind of servant.

clue.text: Victorian reformer making a stir in conversation

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for conversation

parts.note: a chat is an informal conversation

indicators.note: making suggests the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A Victorian radical causing a commotion in a discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chartists campaigned for parliamentary reform in 1830s-50s Britain, so a Chartist is a Victorian reformer.

clue.text: Generous, as the one I write with in the dictionary

indicators.note: in places the writing words inside the dictionary's abbreviation

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
a pen is a writing implement
the hand holding the pen does the writing

explanation.surface: A claim that the writer's own hand is defined as generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-handed means giving freely, a synonym for generous.

clue.text: First and second, say, said about row

indicators.note: about means the word for spoken goes around the noise

parts.note: oral means spoken
a din is a noisy row

explanation.surface: Positions in a race, spoken about a row.
explanation.definitionFit: First and second are ordinal numbers, giving order rather than quantity; these are examples.

clue.text: Change the ebb?

parts.note: an ebb is the sea's flow going back, and writing that flow's four-letter name backwards gives a word for alter

explanation.surface: Asking whether the tide has turned.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the sea's tide backwards, as an ebb runs back, and you get a word meaning change.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to alter a text, a synonym for change.

clue.text: It's a sin — I got cold milk in bark — that's novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are formed into a new order

parts.words: I got cold milk in bark

explanation.surface: Protesting the wickedness of chilled milk spiked in tree bark.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes the book itself: Atticus Finch says it is a sin to do this. 'novel' also nods at what the answer is.
explanation.definitionFit: The title completes the novel's line that shooting a harmless songbird is wrong.

clue.text: King George's volcano on the border

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
Etna is the volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: A king's volcano sits at the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Gretna is the Scottish town just over the English border, famous for runaway weddings.

clue.text: Part of dream about big bird with butter not melting in mouth?

definitions.text: with butter not melting in mouth?

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word goes around the bird
part of means only some of the word is used, its end dropped

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: Dreaming of a big bird with butter that won't melt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone looking as if butter wouldn't melt in their mouth seems modest and coy, an idiom.

clue.text: Time in recent weeks to drop one's cover

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
ult., short for ultimo, means in last month

explanation.surface: A recent period of shedding one's cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds and animals moult by shedding feathers, fur or skin, their natural covering.

clue.text: Begin to wreck sound of Enterprise?

indicators.note: sound of means the phrase is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: to begin is to start, followed by wreck

explanation.surface: Beginning to destroy the noise of a business venture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Enterprise is the starship of the long-running TV series, so the series is clued by example.

clue.text: See 21
Modern liturgy is calling for painful problem

indicators.note: calling means the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: modern is new, a liturgy is a rite, then is

explanation.surface: A new church service is said to cause pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuritis is inflammation of a nerve, a painful medical condition.

clue.text: A style of fabric I can use, if I take it as I please

parts.note: twill is a weave giving diagonal ribs in cloth

explanation.surface: Choosing a fabric I may use whenever I like.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something at will is to do it whenever one likes, an idiom.

clue.text: Scope non-existent at the Equator?

definitions.meaning: the angular distance north or south is zero on the Equator

explanation.surface: Room to manoeuvre that vanishes at the Equator.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude means freedom or leeway, and also the geographic measure that is zero at the Equator.

clue.text: Being sick of banana, use apricots

indicators.note: of means the answer is taken out of the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Feeling ill from eating banana and apricots.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is the feeling of wanting to vomit, being sick.
